headline: Former Australian prime minister Kevin Rudd has urged the United States and China to agree on a minimum set of AI guardrails.
score_reason: New, but one commentator's views at a dinner talk.
importance_line: It adds an experienced diplomat's voice to the case for US-China AI safety rules, but it is opinion, not policy.
summary: MediaNama reports that Kevin Rudd, former Australian prime minister and president of the Asia Society, told a New Delhi dinner on 6 Oct 2026 that the US and China, which dominate frontier AI, could agree on minimum "de minimis guardrails", saying both capitals now see autonomous AI agents as a shared danger and pointing to a recent article by China's security minister Chen Yixin that blames the US while calling the danger real. These are Rudd's views, not government positions; he called the Trump-Xi summit's line that a channel is now open between the capitals the one encouraging sign.
notes: Headline mentions four guardrails; they were not in the page text, so not listed. Context: today's C13-02 reports Trump rejecting joint AI work with China.
